column1: # cut_trigger_reachability_baseline.tsv
# 2026-08-28: the two rows for this gate's OWN workflow and script were
# removed, not edited, because the gap they recorded is CLOSED -- the
# workflow now carries `tags: ['v1.*']`. Leaving them would let a revert of
# that trigger hide behind its own baseline, which is the one thing a
# baseline must never do.
# AXIS THREE of scripts/verify_declared_gates_reachable.sh. Each row is a file
# that declares itself cut-blocking, IS reachable on axis one, and is NOT
# reachable from any entry point that fires on a v1.0.* tag push.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FLIP. Re-seeding the existing verdict with
# tag-aware entry points would turn every row below into an orphan at once and
# block every cut. A gate that does that gets commented out, which lands its
# population right back where it started. So the state on 2026-08-27 is
# RECORDED here and only GROWTH fails. The baseline may SHRINK freely.
# A ROW IS NOT AN EXCUSE. It is a note that nobody has decided yet. Every row
# is UNREVIEWED because I measured the gap, not the intent -- inventing twelve
# justifications would have made the file look settled when it is not.
# TO CLEAR A ROW, do one of:
#   (a) wire the gate to a runner that fires on a v1.0.* tag, then delete the
#       row -- this is the outcome the axis exists to produce; or
#   (b) replace UNREVIEWED with a real reason, and sign it.
# Two of these were MEASURED executing zero times at the commit v1.0.48 was cut
# from (#1167): customer-download-path.yml and default-sources-requested.yml,
# whose workflows carry a `paths:` filter ON TOP of a branch-only trigger, so
# even the "it ran on main at that SHA" defence does not hold for them.
# path
.github/workflows/customer-download-path.yml
